text:
Anna K: Heads-up: nightly restore smoke for staging failed. KMS Decrypt error when restoring DB snapshot from s3://redwood-backups/staging/2026-03-10-23. Error snippet: "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt". Anyone seen this after key maintenance?

ops-bot: restore-job #723 FAILED - AccessDenied on KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/6a7b8c9d-... (attached CloudTrail event id xxxxx).

Devon R: Likely scenario: the snapshot was encrypted with an old CMK and we recently rotated to a new CMK alias. If the IAM principal doing the restore doesn't have kms:Decrypt on the older key ID, decrypt will fail.

Miguel S: Confirmed in CloudTrail: kms:Decrypt were Deny for principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner on 2026-03-11T07:12:03Z. The snapshot metadata doesn't currently record the key-id used at time of upload. That makes automated fallback harder.

Zoe L: RBAC angle: who currently has iam permission to add kms:Decrypt to a CMK? We need a tighter process for granting decrypt during key rotations. Also want audit entry when alias->new-key changes.

Devon R: Quick fixes: 1) Temporarily add kms:Decrypt for restore-runner role to the old key policy (fast). 2) Or copy the object and re-encrypt with the new key (or SSE-S3) then attempt restore. Example CLI to re-encrypt by copying to a temp bucket with SSE-S3: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/staging/2026-03-10-23/pg-snapshot.tar.gz \
  s3://temp-unencrypted-backups/pg-snapshot.tar.gz --sse AES256
```
Then restore from the temp bucket. That avoids dealing with old CMK perms.

Anna K: Is copying to SSE-S3 allowed for backups with PII? We should check compliance — previously we required SSE-KMS for certain datasets.

Zoe L: For PII we need SSE-KMS and key usage records. SSE-S3 removes KMS audit trail so not ideal for regulated snapshots. Only ok as emergency short-term workaround; escalate to compliance if used.

Miguel S: Operational improvement: add a "kms_key_id" metadata blob to each snapshot manifest at upload time. That way restore runner can choose the right key policy check or select copy workflow automatically. Also add a pre-check step that verifies decrypt permission via a dry-run kms:Decrypt call.

Devon R: Long-term approach: use alias promotion pattern instead of creating new keys in place without tracking. When rotating, keep old key policies allowing a short window of decrypt for restore principals, then revoke after validation. Also tag keys with rotation-id and keep alias history in Dynamo table.

Anna K: We had a failed restore in staging only; production unaffected so far. I opened INC-2026-045 to track. Immediate action: please apply temp decrypt grant to old key for restore-runner so nightly can complete.

Zoe L: I'll draft a mini-runbook for key rotation: required RBAC approvals, how to grant temporary decrypt, how to record alias changes in audit log, and when to re-encrypt snapshots. Will put draft in the ticket.

Miguel S: I'll add kms_key_id to snapshot manifests and a preflight kms:Decrypt dry-run step for the restore pipeline. Target PR by EOD tomorrow.

Devon R: I'll add a fallback step to the restore workflow: on kms:Decrypt AccessDenied -> attempt copy-to-temp with SSE-KMS specifying new key (if compliance allows) or alert SRE for manual intervention.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: patch/restore-fallback will run integration tests on staging once PRs are merged.

Anna K: Action items recap: Anna -> coordinate temp grant and confirm compliance ok for any SSE-S3 emergency use (owner: Anna). Miguel -> manifest + preflight (owner: Miguel). Devon -> add fallback copy workflow + tests (owner: Devon). Zoe -> RBAC/runbook + audit requirements (owner: Zoe).

Devon R: Also recommend we add a CloudWatch alarm for repeated kms:Decrypt Deny spikes so we catch this quicker.

Anna K: Thanks all. Filing follow-ups in INC-2026-045 and assigning. If anyone sees other restore failures, drop logs in the ticket. :thumbsup:
